title: Multicast peering escape-hatch diverges from C: no scope>=3/hop-limit gating in Rust
description: P3 from correctness codereview of worker6-b7z9.39 (BR multicast drop, spec 04 6.3.4). Default-off drop semantics match C exactly. But with multicast_peering ENABLED, C still gates backbone-ingress relay on scope >= 3 && hop_limit > 1 and applies forwarded_hop_limit (lichen/subsys/lichen/routing/router.c:524-552 — link-scope ff01/ff02 multicast is delivered local-only, never relayed); the Rust guard forwards ANY multicast scope at any hop limit unmodified when peering is on (rust/lichen-gateway/src/gateway.rs upstream_to_mesh; the end_to_end test codifies ff02::1a forwarding with peering on, which C would deliver local-only). Since multicast peering is explicitly-configured future work (no production caller sets the flag yet), this is latent. Fix when wiring peering config into lichend: mirror the C scope>=3/hop_limit>1 relay gating and forwarded_hop_limit application, and align the test (use a global-scope multicast for the forward assertion). Also note the C reference lines moved: the multicast boundary logic is at router.c:524-552, not the :576-589 cited in worker6-b7z9.39.
